summary: Edge slab saturation causing ephemeral worker throttling and elevated 502s for tenant NimbleDocs
description: Issue summary: Around 2026-03-10 08:40 UTC we started seeing an elevated rate of 502 responses for a small subset of NimbleDocs requests. Impact: ~6% error rate (502) for the customer's production routes, intermittent but persistent for ~90 minutes, affecting chat and small-batch embedding endpoints. Environment: prod (us-east), Dedicated pool tenant pinned to nv4-family nodes. Symptoms: API Gateway returning 502 upstream errors; runtime logs show ephemeral worker eviction and threadpool timeouts; edge telemetry reports slab (connection accept queue) near-saturation and large backlog of half-closed sockets. Customer reports user-facing failures and slow retries.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a mixed workload for tenant NimbleDocs: 60% short-chat requests (~150-300 token prompts) and 40% small embedding batches (batch size 8) at ~220 rps.
2) Observe accept queue depth on edge proxies for routes mapped to NimbleDocs increase above 400 connections.
3) Watch responses from API Gateway flip from 200 to 502 with increased upstream connection resets and 'runtime-worker-evict' messages in runtime logs.
4) Reproduce reliably during a sustained 10-15 minute ramp where autoscaler does not add capacity fast enough.
Notes: load generator and tenant headers used in reproduction attached to related GH PR.
logs: [2026-03-10T08:42:03Z] apigw: upstream response 502 tenant=NimbleDocs route=/v1/chat err=upstream-reset
[2026-03-10T08:42:05Z] runtime[worker-17]: eviction triggered: reason=ephemeral-worker-throttle active_conn=320 cpu_ms=98
investigation_notes: Initial triage by Support (A. Martinez) and SRE (L. Chen): correlated apigw telemetry and runtime metrics. Key observations: high accept_queue_depth on edge proxies coincides with increased ephemeral worker evictions inside the serving runtime. Autoscaler lag: dedicated pool did not scale up during the ramp because prewarm budget exhausted. Threadpool metrics show steady queue growth and several task timeouts. Hypothesis: edge slab (accept queue) saturation plus keepalive churn is creating bursts of half-closed sockets; this causes the runtime to throttle ephemeral workers and run into threadpool timeouts, producing upstream resets and 502s. No model code change or recent config roll detected for tenant. Cross-referenced Slack thread #support-ops (https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C02ABC123).
mitigation: Short-term mitigation applied at 2026-03-10T09:02 UTC: 1) Applied conservative rate cap on NimbleDocs routes at the API Gateway to limit peak rps and reduce accept queue growth. 2) Increased edge proxy accept queue size for the affected nodes by one step (temporary knob). 3) Triggered manual scale-up of dedicated pool by adding 2 warm NVidia nodes. Immediate effect: 502 rate dropped from 6% to ~0.8% within 3 minutes.
resolution: Status: Partial mitigation in place; customer impact reduced. Root cause under investigation — likely interaction between edge accept-queue saturation and serving-runtime ephemeral throttling under mixed chat+embedding traffic. Next steps: 1) SRE to add a short-term autoscaler holdback change to prefer scale-up over prewarm in similar bursts (owner: SRE team). 2) Runtime team to investigate task queue backpressure behavior and improve worker eviction heuristics (owner: runtime squad, related PR linked). 3) Create permanent runbook entry and dashboard widgets (owner: support/observability). 4) Follow up with NimbleDocs with RCA and compensating credits. Target full RCA and permanent mitigations by 2026-03-18.
